newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler chief pledges profit, sales increases.
newsitem.headline: Daimler chief pledges profit, sales increases.

text.p: Daimler-Benz AG Chairman Juergen Schrempp promised shareholders on Wednesday that the company would have "substantial" increases in profits and sales this year.
"The group is now active in businesses marked above all by healthy, self-sustaining growth and high profit potential," he said in an address to shareholders.

Only a year ago, Schrempp went before angry shareholders to apologise for racking up the biggest loss in German corporate history and for not being able to pay a dividend for the first time in more than four decades.
This year, Daimler management received congratulations from shareholders who encouraged them to stay what has at times been a difficult course.
The bright outlook comes amid growing confidence that a sweeping reorganization earlier this year will result in a more efficient management structure.
Also, company sales in the first four months of this year were up 15 percent from year-earlier levels.

"Although this year will be dominated by numerous product launches along with the implementation of programmes to optimize business operations, we assume that we can achieve a substantial improvement in operating profit," Schrempp said.
Daimler-Benz, Germany's largest company, reported an operating profit for 1996 of 2.423 billion marks ($1.4 billion), up from a loss of 7.197 billion marks in 1995.
Schrempp said sales for 1997 should be "substantially" above last year's 106.34 billion marks.
In the first four months of 1997, Daimler said group sales jumped 15 percent from a year earlier, to 36.3 billion marks, as all of the company's major divisions posted higher turnover.

The backbone of Daimler-Benz, its Mercedes-Benz car and truck business, showed double-digit sales growth in the four months. Passenger car sales climbed 14 percent to 16.2 billion marks, while commercial vehicle sales advanced 15 percent to 11.6 billion marks.

Schrempp said he expected to sell more than 700,000 cars this year, a record high, and that Daimler's share of the world car market should climb to 2.2 percent in the coming years from 1.6 percent now.
